data.title: SpectralGPT: Spectral Remote Sensing Foundation Model
data.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

journal.name: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

data.abstract: The foundation model has recently garnered significant attention due to its potential to revolutionize the field of visual representation learning in a self-supervised manner. While most foundation models are tailored to effectively process RGB images for various visual tasks, there is a noticeable gap in research focused on spectral data, which offers valuable information for scene understanding, especially in remote sensing (RS) applications. To fill this gap, we created for the first time a universal RS foundation model, named SpectralGPT, which is purpose-built to handle spectral RS images using a novel 3D generative pretrained transformer (GPT). Compared to existing foundation models, SpectralGPT 1) accommodates input images with varying sizes, resolutions, time series, and regions in a progressive training fashion, enabling full utilization of extensive RS Big Data; 2) leverages 3D token generation for spatial-spectral coupling; 3) captures spectrally sequential patterns via multi-target reconstruction; and 4) trains on one million spectral RS images, yielding models with over 600 million parameters. Our evaluation highlights significant performance improvements with pretrained SpectralGPT models, signifying substantial potential in advancing spectral RS Big Data applications within the field of geoscience across four downstream tasks: single/multi-label scene classification, semantic segmentation, and change detection.

journal.name: IGARSS 2025 - 2025 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium

data.abstract: Foundation models (FMs), owing to their strong generalization capabilities, extract more universal features that are less prone to noise. This offers a solution to cross-domain hyperspectral image (HSI) classification by simply fine-tuning FM on source domain (SD) in a supervised manner and then testing it on target domain (TD). However, HSIs captured under different conditions exhibit significant discrepancies, and even FMs like SpectralGPT[1] can be heavily affected by the domain shift. To further enhance the performance of FMs on TD, we propose a method named Masked Spatial-Spectral Consistency (MSSC) based on self-training framework. MSSC applies 3D random masking to TD images and enforces the consistency between predictions of student network on masked images and predictions of teacher network on corresponding unmasked images. Experimental results show that our MSSC improves the overall accuracy (OA) of TD by 2.8% on the Houston dataset, reaching 76.6%, outperforming most methods, and achieves the best OA on the HyRANK dataset with a 6.4% improvement, reaching 64.2%.
